Vijayawada, November 3: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu continued to disrupt normal life in coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday, with heavy rainfall delaying urban local body election vote counting in Vijayawada and slowing the process in Guntur. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for the state.
In Vijayawada, vote counting began nearly two-and-a-half hours behind schedule due to heavy rain. Officials initially counted postal ballots, while votes were being counted ward-wise in separate halls for the East, West and Central constituencies.
The cyclone has also caused significant damage to agricultural fields and salt pans in and around Ongole. Heavy rainfall and strong winds have disrupted salt production and damaged standing crops, causing substantial losses to farmers and salt pan workers.
Railway services have also been affected. The South Coast Railway's Vijayawada Division temporarily suspended train movement on the Vijayawada-Ongole-Gudur section after gale-force winds were recorded at Karavadi Station. A total of 29 trains were regulated, while several others were cancelled, diverted or rescheduled due to adverse weather conditions. Railway authorities have advised passengers to cooperate, reiterating that safety remains their top priority.
Meanwhile, vote counting in NTR district began at 8 am despite heavy rainfall. District Collector Dr G Lakshmisha said counting was progressing peacefully across all five local bodies, with adequate police security arrangements in place.
He said officials, election agents and other staff were cooperating to ensure a free and fair counting process.
Counting of votes for 92 urban local bodies across Andhra Pradesh also began on Tuesday. The exercise covers 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities and Nagar Panchayats. Polling for these elections was held on November 1, from 7 am to 5 pm.

Andhra Pradesh: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu over south coastal Andhra Pradesh continued to affect normal activities on Tuesday, with heavy rainfall delaying urban local body election vote counting in Vijayawada and slowing the process in Guntur. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for Andhra Pradesh.
In Vijayawada, vote counting for the local body elections began around two-and-a-half hours late due to heavy rains. Officials initially took up the counting of postal ballots, while counting was conducted in separate halls ward-wise for the East, West and Central constituencies.
The cyclone has also affected agricultural and allied activities in the coastal region. Salt pans and agricultural fields in and around Ongole have suffered extensive damage due to Murasu. Heavy rains and strong winds have severely affected salt production and damaged standing crops, leaving farmers and salt pan workers facing significant losses.
Railway operations have also been affected by the cyclone and associated heavy rainfall. In a passenger advisory issued on Tuesday, South Coast Railway’s Vijayawada Division announced the temporary suspension of train movement on the Vijayawada-Ongole-Gudur section following gale-force winds recorded at Karavadi Station.
Train services on the section are being regulated at originating and en-route stations until further notice. A total of 29 trains have been regulated, while certain services have been cancelled, diverted or rescheduled due to cyclone-related conditions.
Passengers have been requested to cooperate, with railway authorities expressing regret over the inconvenience and reiterating that passenger safety remains their priority.
Earlier, despite the delay, counting in the NTR district began at 8 am, with agents and staff reaching the centres on time despite the rains.
NTR District Collector Dr G Lakshmisha said counting was proceeding peacefully across the district’s five local bodies.
“The counting of votes for the local body elections is underway in the NTR district. In the entire district, the local body election counting process has started. We have five local bodies… Everything is going peacefully… Police security is in place everywhere… Everyone is cooperating… The spirit of the free and fair elections is upheld,” he told ANI.
Counting for elections to 92 urban local bodies across Andhra Pradesh also began on Tuesday, covering 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
The elections were held on November 1, with polling conducted from 7 am to 5 pm.

Storm disrupts election counting and forces school closures in TN
Dubai: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu battered coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday, bringing torrential rain and winds gusting up to 120km/h, disrupting train services, damaging crops and delaying vote counting in local elections as authorities issued red alerts and stepped up emergency operations.
The cyclone crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole between 3.30am and 5.30am, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The storm made landfall with sustained winds of 100–110km/h, gusting to 120km/h, before moving north-northwestwards and gradually weakening.
The IMD issued red alerts for three districts and orange alerts for other affected areas, warning of continued heavy rainfall. Fishermen were advised not to venture into the sea for two days.
Railway operations were severely affected after gale-force winds were recorded at Karavadi station.
South Coast Railway’s Vijayawada Division temporarily suspended train movements along the Vijayawada-Ongole-Gudur section, affecting 29 trains.
Several services were cancelled, diverted or rescheduled, while others were regulated at originating and intermediate stations.
Railway authorities said passenger safety remained their priority and urged travellers to cooperate with officials.
Heavy rainfall also disrupted road transport, prompting Andhra Pradesh Transport Minister Mandipalli Ramprasad Reddy to direct officials to suspend bus services wherever necessary and operate vehicles only on safe routes.
Agricultural areas around Ongole suffered extensive damage, with strong winds and heavy rain destroying standing crops and affecting salt production.
Salt pans were inundated, leaving farmers and workers facing significant financial losses.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority reported exceptionally heavy rainfall in several coastal areas.
Naguluppalapadu in Prakasam district recorded 198.01mm of rainfall between Monday morning and early Tuesday, while Kothapatnam received 182.25mm.
Bapatla recorded 128.53mm, Chirala 124.10mm and Ongole Urban nearly 107mm.
Authorities warned that further heavy to extremely heavy rainfall could affect Guntur, Krishna, Palnadu, NTR, Eluru and West Godavari districts.
The cyclone also disrupted counting of votes in Andhra Pradesh’s urban local body elections.
In Vijayawada, counting began about two-and-a-half hours late because of heavy rain, while operations in Guntur were also slowed.
In Machilipatnam, strong winds blew away tents erected at a counting centre at Krishna University.
Special buses were arranged to transport election staff, while municipal workers carried out emergency repairs.
Counting was underway for elections to 92 urban local bodies, including 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha said the situation remained under control and no untoward incidents had been reported.
He urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel and follow official safety instructions.
Emergency teams were deployed to clear uprooted trees and monitor vulnerable areas, including the Budameru catchment.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and assured him of full central assistance.
Shah said National Disaster Response Force and State Disaster Response Force teams were already conducting relief operations.
Naidu briefed him on crop losses and property damage caused by successive cyclones.
Karnataka also offered assistance, including the deployment of 500 skilled workers and equipment to help restore electricity infrastructure damaged by the earlier Cyclone Arnab.
Murasu’s impact extended into neighbouring Tamil Nadu, where heavy rain and thunderstorms forced schools to close in parts of Cuddalore district.
Authorities warned residents against travelling through waterlogged roads as unsettled weather continued across northern Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.
